idPrefix.description: Story ID prefix: S gives S-001 and scenarios S-001.1.

storiesDir.description: Folder holding one sub-folder per story, named <ID>-<slug>.

storyMayImport.description: Path prefixes story code may import, besides its own folder.

storyTestMayAlsoImport.description: Extra path prefixes story tests may import.

wiring.description: Files allowed to import stories (composition roots).

layers.description: For each folder, the path prefixes its files may import. The longest matching folder applies.

portsDir.description: Where port interfaces live; each exported interface should have an adapter.

gapsOnlyWarnFor.description: Statuses whose missing code or tests are warnings instead of errors.

mustPassFor.description: Statuses that require every scenario test to pass.

testCommand.description: Command that runs the tests and writes its report(s) to testReport.

testReport.description: Where testCommand writes its report: Vitest/Jest JSON or JUnit XML, recognised from the content. A list reads several reports (for example pytest's and a conformance suite's); a listed report that wasn't written is skipped.

storyTemplateDir.description: Folder of story templates (story.md, spec.md). Built-in templates are used when it does not exist.

exemptStatuses.description: Statuses listed in the trace but exempt from every story rule.

rules.description: Severity per rule name, overriding the default. "off" drops the rule.

tiers.description: Where scenarios can be proven. local runs testCommand (or its own command) on every trace; another tier with a command runs on `storyspec trace --tier <name>` and its results are recorded in stories/PROOF.json; a tier with no command (manual) is proven with `storyspec prove`.

command.description: Runs the tier's tests, with STORYSPEC_TIER set to the tier's name.

report.description: Where the command writes its report(s); defaults to testReport.

defaultProof.description: The tiers a scenario must be proven in, unless its story (proof: in story.md) or its tag ({#S-001.1 proof=…}) says otherwise.
